source.title: Tensegrity frameworks: Dynamic analysis review and open problems

accepted.question_text: How can a tensegrity framework be designed by generating a new topology, including which nodes are connected, which kind of edge is used for each connection, the spatial nodal configuration, and the edge stresses, so that the resulting structure achieves a desired performance criterion such as stiffness, stiffness-to-mass ratio, or deformation under external forces while satisfying the geometrical and statical constraints required for a feasible tensegrity realization?

evidence.page: ScienceDirect HTML section: Design for tensegrity structures
evidence.quote: means the generation of new topologies

accepted.question_text: For a tensegrity structure whose feasible configurations are embedded in a lower-dimensional subspace of the chosen parameterization space, how can one compute a shape-control or path-planning trajectory between two feasible configurations, taking into account environmental and internal constraints such as non-intersecting bars and the robot kinematic and dynamic models?

evidence.page: IRI PDF section 5: Shape control for tensegrity structures
evidence.quote: all possible feasible configurations of a tensegrity structure are embedded in a subspace of lower dimension than the parameterization space.

accepted.question_text: For tensegrity structures whose desired set point or path has already been chosen by form finding, static design, or dynamic path planning, what passive or active control techniques can compensate for inaccuracies or absence of a dynamic model and for unknown external perturbations, so that the structure does not oscillate when it should remain still and can follow the desired path?

evidence.page: ScienceDirect HTML section: Control of tensegrity structures
evidence.quote: The main issues regarding the control of tensegrity structures are associated to its dynamic model.
